title: The later Thomists deny any middle knowledge besides natural and free knowledge
source_text: XIX. Veruntamen non pauci Doctores Scholae Romanae, & praesertim illi qui Thomistae recentiores dicuntur, praeter scientiam naturalem, quae dicitur scientia simplicis intelligentiae, & scientiam liberam, quae scientia visionis vocatur, negant in Deo dari scientiam ullam mediam, per quam scilicet, ante omne voluntatis suae decretum, Deus noverit ea quae nec simpliciter possibilia sunt, nec etiam sunt absolute futura, sed futura essent sub hac, vel illa conditione, & a creaturis intelligentibus hoc, vel illo dato libere fierent.
pass_a_gloss: XIX. Nevertheless not a few Doctors of the Roman School, and especially those who are called the more recent Thomists, besides natural knowledge, which is called knowledge of simple intelligence, and free knowledge, which is called knowledge of vision, deny that there is given in God any middle knowledge, by which namely, before every decree of his will, God would know those things which neither are simply possible, nor yet are absolutely future, but would be future under this, or that condition, and would be done freely by intelligent creatures, this, or that being given.
pass_b_english: Yet a good number of teachers of the Roman school, especially those called the later Thomists, deny that God has any middle knowledge. Besides natural knowledge, called the knowledge of simple intelligence, and free knowledge, called the knowledge of vision, they admit no third kind.

They deny any knowledge by which God, before every decree of his will, would know things that are neither merely possible nor absolutely future, but that would happen under this or that condition, done freely by intelligent creatures given this or that.

choices.why: The Molinist technical term; 'middle knowledge' is the established English name and is kept throughout.
